verdict.reason:

- 4.4: profile, no cape.
- 5.3: no cape.
- 8.2: no cape.

So the costume changes from page to page within a single continuous scene, and the cape is easy to see at print size, most of all in 2.2 and 6.1. verdict.reason:
This is partly confirmed, but it is minor, not major.

The table moving is refuted. In 5.3 the camera is lower and turned, so the table sits at the left with Nagoji's stool between it and the brazier. Panels 6.1 and 6.2 use the same set-up: table at left, stool in the middle, brazier to the right. So this is a change of camera angle, not a rebuilt room.

Two prop changes do hold up when zoomed in:
- **Brazier in 5.3:** 5.1 shows a low tripod basket brazier. 6.1 and 6.2 repeat that same design. 5.3 (about x 990-1080, y 1580-1750) swaps it for a tall black four-legged pedestal brazier.

Why minor: the script beat is still met. The table is neat and evenly spaced, with pliers, hammers and wedges, and the extra items break no rule in the script or the continuity bible. No character identity or lettering is affected. Readers usually take an insert as a closer, more detailed view. Brazier designs also change across the chapter anyway: the bowl brazier in 6.4 and 8.4, and the basket brazier in 8.3 and 8.5. So the 5.3 pedestal reads as set-dressing drift, not a broken beat. If 5.3 is regenerated, give it the 5.1 tripod basket brazier, and trim the 5.2 props to match 5.1.

A wall chain runs from a ring to his ankle irons. refuted.reason: I zoomed into panels 6.4, 6.1, 6.2 and 5.1, and the reported drift does not hold up. (1) Brazier: in 6.4 the fire sits in a vessel with a spiked rim, the same shape as the tripod basket brazier in 5.1. The bottom panel border cuts it off just under the rim, so the legs are simply out of frame. Nothing shows a low pan sitting on the floor. Its spot between Nagoji and João also matches 6.2, where the brazier is on the viewer's right of Nagoji. (2) Tongs: João lifts them off the edge of a wooden table covered in iron tools. The script only says "off the table", and at print size it reads as the tool table. This is a tighter angle, not a second piece of furniture a reader would notice. (3) Wall shackles: they hang on a stretch of wall beside the door that 5.1 and 6.1 never show (in 5.1 that area is past the panel's right edge). Neither the script nor CONTINUITY.md fixes the chamber's wall dressing; the script calls only for the vault, ceiling ropes, a brazier and a table. Chains on the wall of a torture chamber are normal set dressing for a new camera angle. The script beat is all there (João not looking up, tongs in hand, both lines with tails pointing to him). Whatever variation remains is too small to matter.

refuted.description: Same-moment continuity break with 8.3. The brazier is a large iron cauldron of coals at João's hip, but in 8.3 and 8.6 it is a small tripod basket by the back wall. Nagoji, in the background, sits against a wall hung with chains beside a table, his hands unbound in his lap and well away from the brazier. In 8.3 he is on the stool in the middle of the room with João working at his hands.
refuted.reason:
I zoomed into 8.3, 8.5 and 8.6 on page-08.png. The claimed continuity break doesn't hold up.

(1) The braziers are not different-sized objects. In 8.3 the brazier is a round iron bowl of coals on legs, with banded sides and rim loops, standing against the back-left wall. It is roughly as wide as João's torso, so it is not a "small tripod basket". In 8.5 the same kind of round iron bowl is shown as a foreground close-up next to João's hand, so it looks bigger only because of perspective. The script says "João's hand reaching for the brazier", so he has walked over to it and it is at his hip. The real difference is detail only: a solid rim with a scroll handle in 8.5 against banded sides in 8.3. At print size the 8.3 brazier is about 1.5 cm across, so that is polish at most.

(2) The object in 8.6 is a separate small wall fire-basket by the door, a light source. It is not meant to be the brazier.

(3) Nagoji in 8.5 is where the staging puts him. He is on the same stool, barefoot, with the same ankle shackles and chain and the same white wrist bandages as in 8.3. Neither panel shows wrist ropes, so "no wrist ropes" is not a change. He is no longer having his hands worked on because João has stepped away to the brazier. That is the point of the beat ("Nagoji, blurred, in the background"), and the art does blur him with shallow focus. The wall chains and table behind him are a reverse angle on a part of the vault that 8.3's high-angle shot doesn't fully show, which is a normal cinematic cheat. The table and the door on the right are also roughly consistent with 8.3's layout.

His calm, slumped seated pose fits the 8.4 caption about the mind floating above the body. Nothing here is a wrong identity, a costume break or a missing beat that would justify "major".

A 4x crop of page 9, inset 2 (original px about 777-925 x 1145-1575) shows a red cloth with an off-white band and a brass clasp. It is a sliver about 25-30 px wide at 300 DPI, cut off by the inset's right border. Below it is a red strip that looks like a coat lining or a second garment beside a brass tube. The man holding the keys is clearly dressed in a brown coat with brass buttons, a cream shirt and a wide leather belt, which fits the bible and João's approved sheet (brown leather, cream shirt, wide belt, iron key ring). Nothing shows a red coat body, red sleeves, crossbelts or a British cut, and the red is not clearly his garment at all. It could belong to someone behind him, or be a sash or lining. At a 6x9 print size (about 150 px per inch), the inset is about 1.3 in wide and the red-white sliver is about 0.15 in. It reads as a scrap of coloured cloth at the frame edge, not a uniform. The bible rule (CONTINUITY.md line 128) bans guards that read as British redcoats. A fragment of red trim or lining at the edge of a brown-coated figure does not do that. It also does not clash with the guards in inset 1 or on page 4, panel 1, because the visible guard is in brown like them. At most this is optional polish: the strip could be recoloured brown or cropped out so it stays consistent with the brown-and-cream guard palette. It is not a major costume error.

minors.description: Duarte's cassock changes from panel to panel. In some panels he wears a short shoulder cape that the approved sheet does not have. In other panels (4.2, 4.4, 5.3, 7.2, 8.3) he wears the plain sheet cassock.
minors.evidence: A layered shoulder cape is visible on 2.1, 2.2, 3.5 and 6.1 (6.1 crop: the cape falls over both arms above the hands holding the paper). On 4.2 the full figure shows the plain buttoned cassock with sash and no cape, which matches the sheet's front and turnaround views.

minors.description: Duarte's face drifts from his sheet in this panel. The face is fuller and softer, the nose is broader, and the hair is a sandy blond-grey. It is no longer the gaunt, hollow-cheeked man with steel-grey curls from the sheet and from 4.2, 7.2 and 8.6.
minors.evidence: In a 2x crop of the crouched priest (about x 470 to 620, y 262 to 400) and the Duarte lineup across 2.2, 3.1, 3.5, 4.2, 6.1, 7.2, 7.5 and 8.6, 3.1 is the outlier. The cheek is rounded, the nose bulbous and the hair light and tawny. Every other panel keeps the sheet's sharp nose and grey swept curls.

minors.description: In the high wide shot, Duarte's collar seems to show a thin white strip at the throat. That reads as the white Roman collar tab the bible bans as a 19th-century anachronism.
minors.evidence: At 5x on the small standing priest (about x 755 to 805, y 495 to 545) there is a pale white line along the front edge of the black standing collar. The bible's Duarte line reads 'NO white Roman collar tab'. The figure is small, but the strip is the brightest mark on the collar.

minors.description: The off-panel tail points the wrong way. Duarte's question tail exits to the right, but on 3.1 Duarte crouches on the viewer's left of Nagoji, and in this panel Nagoji looks toward the viewer's left.
minors.evidence: The balloon 'You understand our language, senhor marata?' has its tail at the right panel border, at about (1180,620). On 3.1 Duarte is at x of about 440 to 600, to the left of Nagoji at about 760 to 880.

minors.description: Awkward crop on Joao's face. The panel's top border cuts through his brow, and the speech balloon covers his cheek, so his face is only partly visible in this panel.
minors.evidence: A crop of the top of the panel (about y 920 to 1100) shows his head cut at eye level by the top border. The 'Este. This one is stubborn.' balloon covers the left side of his face, and the beard and one eye are all that read clearly.

minors.description: Nagoji's bandaging changes within the page. In 4.1 (and 3.1) the wraps cover his hands across the knuckles. In 4.2 and 4.4 only narrow wrist bands remain and the hands are bare. The chapter 1 bible row specifies bandaged hands and wrists.
minors.evidence: 4.1: wraps over the backs of both hands as the guards haul him up. 4.2: short white cuffs at the wrists only, bare hands and fingers. 4.4: the same wrist-only bands.

minors.description: Nagoji's bandages carry rust-red blotches that read as blood. This brushes against the standing rule of no blood or gore; the hands' damage should be implied by grime and staging.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09.png around (600-1100, 560-960): red-brown blotches across the wraps on both hands. Similar red stains on the knuckle wraps in 3.1.

minors.description: Duarte's likeness drifts. In 3.1 his hair is sandy blond-grey and tousled, with a rounder, softer face. In 3.5 his hair reads brown and smoothly combed. The approved sheet and 2.2, 4.2 and 7.2 show grey hair swept back with loose curls on a gaunt, lined face.
minors.evidence: 3.1 crop: warm golden-blond highlights in the hair, fuller cheeks. 3.5: brown slicked hair. 7.2: silver-grey curls and a gaunt face, matching the sheet.

minors.description: In the Kanka memory, the pre-capture Nagoji has visible stubble along his jaw and chin. The bible keeps his chin clean-shaven, with light stubble allowed in captivity only; memory panels set before the capture should show a clean chin.
minors.evidence: Memory figure in the rust-red turban and red sash with his cheek against the black mare: dark stubble texture along the jaw below the moustache.

minors.description: Nagoji's hand bandages are smeared with rust-red stains that read as dried blood seeping through, straight after the torture page. The standing rule is no blood or gore. Turning the stains toward grey-brown grime would keep the aftermath without showing blood. Page 3, panel 1 has smaller red marks on the exposed fingers and bandages.
minors.evidence: Close crop of page 9, panel 1 hands (about x 570-780, y 480-650): reddish-brown streaks wind round both wrapped hands and wrists. Page 3, panel 1 crop at about x 640-790, y 410-510 shows pinkish-red patches on the fingers.

minors.description: Possible anachronism in the writing tool. It has a black pointed tip set in a gold ferrule on a smooth white shaft, which reads more like a metal-nib dip pen or a brush holder than a cut goose quill. For a 1738 Goa clerk the tip should be the cut, split end of the quill itself.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of page 1 at about x 890-1010, y 770-870: a gold band joins the shaft to a dark tapered point.

minors.description: Duarte's ink stains are drawn as large purple-black blotches across the back of his hand and his knuckles. They read as bruises, lesions or blood blisters, not as the ink on a writer's fingertips that the bible calls for. The same blotching shows on page 6, panel 1 and page 4, panel 2.
minors.evidence: Crop of page 7, panel 2 at about x 300-620, y 520-830: round dark violet spots spread over the back of his raised hand. Page 6, panel 1 shows the same spotting on the hand holding the papers.

minors.description: The tail on Duarte's off-panel question stops inside the panel, in the stone wall, instead of reaching the border. It also points screen-right, but in 3.1 Duarte sits to Nagoji's screen-left. The top of the balloon touches the top panel border.
minors.evidence: The 'You understand our language, senhor marata?' tail tip is at about (1637, 867), roughly 50 px short of the right border at x 1688. The top of the balloon is about 2 px below the border at y about 797.

minors.description: The two captions step down from right to left, against the normal reading path. The first caption, 'Above us, the bells rang for evening prayer.', sits mid-right. The second, 'Steady as monsoon rain on a Deccan roof.', sits lower-left. A reader going left to right meets the simile before the line it describes. The approved r6 page 1 puts them left then right on one baseline.
minors.evidence: 'Above us...' box is at about x 1022-1560, y 2306-2393. 'Steady as...' box is at about x 173-691, y 2395-2483.

minors.description: The second caption sits in the middle of the chained row. It covers the torsos and knees of three prisoners, part of the single iron bar the script calls for, and the front of Nagoji's knee. The approved r6 page 1 keeps both captions in the empty wall space above the heads.
minors.evidence: The 'Not with ceremony or proclamation...' box at about x 811-1411, y 565-694 covers the grey-bearded prisoner's body, the hunched prisoner's legs and the ochre tunic hem at Nagoji's knee.

minors.description: The tight mouth shot in 3.3 takes nearly half the page height. That squeezes 3.2, 3.4 and 3.5 into thin strips where João and Duarte are small, and 'Bring him.', the line that closes the page, is spoken by a tiny figure. In the approved r6 page 3, 3.3 takes about a quarter of the page. The right balloon in 3.3 also touches the bottom border.
minors.evidence: 3.3 runs from about y 1044 to y 2048, roughly 1000 of the 2144 px panel area. 3.2, 3.4 and 3.5 are each about 250 px tall. The bottom of the 'But you can speak your questions...' balloon touches the border at about y 2045.

minors.description: The second Duarte balloon is a tall, narrow pill holding eight lines of two or three words each, which reads badly next to the wide first balloon. Its tail ends at Duarte's shoulder, not near his head. 'Viceroy's' in the first balloon uses a straight typewriter apostrophe instead of a typographic one.
minors.evidence: The 'What we do not / know is who / ordered the / attacks, how / ...' balloon is at about x 1341-1650, y 555-1001, and its tail tip is at about (1250, 650), on Duarte's shoulder. The straight apostrophe in 'Viceroy's' is at about (714, 627).

minors.description: Duarte's 'Enough.' and João's off-panel 'He still holds back names.' sit stacked on the right with almost no gap, so they read as one speaker's run, and their tails point in opposite directions. The tail on 'Enough.' stops in empty space by the hanging ropes, well short of Duarte's head. Duarte's closing line is far left at the bottom, so the script order depends only on the vertical stagger.
minors.evidence: 'Enough.' box is at about x 1255-1429, y 2143-2261. The João balloon is at about x 1241-1616, y 2282-2389, a gap of about 20 px. The 'Enough.' tail tip is at about (1150, 2235), about 110 px right of Duarte's hair.

minors.description: Duarte's two balloons are stacked with a hairline gap and have stub tails pointing different ways: one up into the top border, one left into his robe. They would read better as connected balloons with a single tail toward his head off-panel. The second balloon leaves 'quill.' alone on its own line.
minors.evidence: 'Not yet.' box is at about x 215-384, y 1595-1713, with its tail pointing up. 'The Viceroy needs a hand that can still hold a / quill.' is at about x 194-793, y 1724-1897, with its tail pointing left to x about 165.

minors.description: The prisoner's whisper is lettered in a normal solid balloon with no whisper treatment, although the script describes a whisper passing down the line. Its short stub tail ends between Nagoji's shoulder and the whisperer's cupped hand, so at reading size it could be taken as Nagoji speaking.
minors.evidence: The 'They are gathering us for transport. South. By ship. For labour.' balloon is at about x 347-953, y 1775-1953. The tail tip is at about (797, 1750), touching both Nagoji's shoulder and the bandaged prisoner's hand.

minors.description: The script marks the chapter's last line, 'Storms do not ask permission.', as 'CAPTION (separate, weighted)'. It is set in the same box, size and weight as the three captions before it, so the closing line gets no emphasis.
minors.evidence: The 'Storms do not ask permission.' box at about x 932-1325, y 2448-2535 uses the same DIN Condensed size and plain white box as 'They had forgotten the simplest lesson of the Deccan monsoon.' beside it.

minors.description: The full-width caption breaks so that 'the courtyard.' sits alone on a second line, an orphan centred under a page-wide line.
minors.evidence: The caption box spans about x 150-1685, y 1019-1148. Line 1 ends with '...from the stair to' and line 2 is only 'the courtyard.'

minors.description: Several balloons touch panel borders instead of breaking them on purpose or keeping a margin, which looks cramped. In 7.1 and 7.5 the top of the balloon touches the top border. In 7.4 'He seems to favour whoever has the better powder.' is jammed into the bottom-right corner. In 7.2 the first Duarte tail ends at his eye and the second at his ink-stained hand, not toward his mouth.
minors.evidence: 7.1: balloon top at about y 363, border at about y 360. 7.5: balloon top at about y 2222, border at about y 2216. 7.4: balloon right and bottom edges at about x 1678 and y 2205, borders at x 1688 and y 2210. 7.2: tail tips at about (735, 825) on the eye and (756, 957) on the hand.

minors.description: The top border cuts the speaker's head at the brow, and his balloon and humming notes are squeezed into the strip above. João's face reads as truncated next to his own line. In the approved r6 page 2, 2.3 shows his whole head with the balloon in clear wall space.
minors.evidence: The top border at about y 1286 crosses João's forehead; his eyes are at about y 1310. The 'Este. This one is stubborn.' balloon starts at about y 1290, right against the border.

minors.description: The caption overlaps the back of Duarte's head and his shoulder. With the top border already cutting off João's head, the entrance panel reads as two headless figures with a caption pressed on the priest.
minors.evidence: The 'Then Father Duarte came.' box at about x 990-1331, y 392-476 meets Duarte's grey hair and shoulder at about x 971-1026, y 358-480.

minors.description: The caption box overlaps the brim of the left guard's tricorne, and the top border also clips both guards' hats.
minors.evidence: The 'My joints had forgotten the shape of standing.' box at about x 150-710, y 368-462 covers the left end of the hat brim at about x 680-818, y 363-402.

minors.description: 3.2: Duarte's off-panel tail leaves the right edge, but 3.1 put Duarte to Nagoji's left and Nagoji looks left and upward. So his gaze is not 'level' and does not meet the voice. 3.3: the script asks for a mouth that is 'cracked and rust-dark', but the lips are full, smooth and healthy. This giant insert takes about 40 percent of the page and shows no sign of the questioning.
minors.evidence: page-03.png 3.2 (y795-1040): the balloon tail points to the right border at about (1640,860), and Nagoji's eyes turn to screen-left. 3.3 (y1045-2050): clean, unbroken lips under the moustache.

minors.description: The page-turn beat 'His face in profile, lit by that glow' is drawn as a medium-wide escort shot. Nagoji's profile is small and lit cool from the left, not red from the doorway. Duarte stands between him and the glow, so the anticipation on Nagoji's face is lost.
minors.evidence: page-04.png, crop x920-1700, y1960-2545: Nagoji's head is about 60 px tall at the far left, in blue-grey light. The red door is at the far right edge, and Duarte's figure fills the space between them.

minors.description: The script calls this the hesitation beat 'the reader must remember in chapter 24' and says 'Hold on him for a full panel'. Here it is two near-identical half-width thumbnails, the smallest panels on the page. The jaw-working of 8.1 can't be read, and the nod in 8.2 is only a slight extra downward tilt, so the planted beat is underweighted.
minors.evidence: page-08.png y360-590: two panels about 760x230 px each with the same framing. In 8.1 Duarte's lips are pressed and his eyes look down-right; in 8.2 his head is slightly lower with eyes closed. No jaw movement is shown.

minors.description: The script asks for Duarte in the foreground with the calluses on his right hand 'drawn clearly'. Instead Duarte is mid-ground, with Nagoji and prisoners in front and João crowding the right half. João is not in this panel's audited cast. The open right palm shows ink-spotted fingertips but no readable calluses, so the caption about calluses has nothing to point at.
minors.evidence: page-02.png, crop x700-900, y1100-1280, enlarged 3x: a smooth palm with ink dots on the fingertips and no callus ridges. João stands at about x1100-1400 in the same panel. CHAPTER-01-CAST-OVERRIDES.json lists page-02-panel-02 as ["duarte"].

minors.description: The insert does not show the act of entry with ink 'still wet'. 'prisioneiro marata' is set in a clean typeset italic, not wet handwriting, and the quill nib hovers over the blank right-hand page, far from the entry on the left. The 'clerk's' hand also wears a red-and-gold brocade sleeve with a lace ruffle, which reads as a nobleman.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, crop x150-1700, y910-1380: the text '17 prisioneiro marata' is in a uniform Georgia-style italic at about (450,1130). The nib is at about (1250,1190) on the empty right page. A red embroidered cuff with a white lace frill is at the lower right.

minors.description: The script asks for Nagoji nearest us in three-quarter back view. He is drawn three-quarter front, looking over his shoulder straight at the reader. That reveals his face before the 1.3 close-up the page is built around.
minors.evidence: page-01.png 1.1, at about x1250-1530, y380-880: Nagoji faces camera with full face, moustache and ear stud visible.

minors.description: The memory is set on a golden tropical shore at sunset, with palm trees and water. The script asks for 'a winter morning', a Deccan memory, so the Kanka flashback reads as a coastal evening.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, crop x150-1700, y2240-2545: a sun low on the horizon over a lake or sea, a row of coconut palms and a warm orange sky behind the black mare and the turbaned rider.

minors.description: The script asks for a small panel with 'Nagoji's eyes, unfocused. He is not in the room.' The art is a full-width strip with sharp, sideways, suspicious eyes that look very present, so it does not support the caption's 'For an instant the dungeon was gone'.
minors.evidence: page-07.png y1160-1460: a full-width strip with crisp pupils cut hard to screen-right under knitted brows.

minors.description: 9.3 shows Nagoji wide-eyed and alert as the whisper reaches him, which undercuts the 9.4 payoff of 'eyes opening in the dark'. 9.3 is also a warmly torchlit cell with a bright barred window and shafts of daylight, not leaning heads 'in the dark'. The whisper is lettered in a standard solid balloon. The script's final caption, 'Storms do not ask permission' (marked 'separate, weighted'), uses the same box and type as the other captions, so it carries no extra weight.
minors.evidence: page-09.png 9.3 (y1580-1960): Nagoji's eyes are open, two torches burn at the upper left, and a lit barred window is at the upper right. 9.4 (y1960-2545): the 'Storms do not ask permission.' box is the same white box and font size as 'They had forgotten...'.

minors.description: The 'Enough.' tail ends in empty air between Duarte's head and the hanging ropes, not at Duarte. João's off-panel tail ('He still holds back names.') points into the room at the right wall and door, not to the panel edge. The speakers are ambiguous on the page's closing exchange.
minors.evidence: page-08.png, crop x150-1700, y2060-2545: the 'Enough.' tail tip is at about (1140,2240), about 100 px right of Duarte's hair. The 'He still holds back names.' tail tip is at about (1620,2240), inside the panel next to the arched door.
